codex_direct_experiment.description: Codex authored this deterministic CVRP solver directly in the repository. It was not produced through the API evolution loop and was evaluated through the same phase-9 sandbox, validator, and train/holdout split.

meta_patterns.evidence: Mean novelty was high in the game family (0.6092), TSP (0.687611), and CVRP candidate stream (0.771482), yet final wins were domain-dependent.
meta_patterns.interpretation: The loop is good at producing variants; selection and validation determine whether those variants become useful.
meta_patterns.pattern: Syntactic novelty is common, but not sufficient.

meta_patterns.evidence: TSP random replay improved over no replay on final transfer and TSPLIB gaps, while phase 9 improved over weak CVRP baselines but not Clarke-Wright.
meta_patterns.interpretation: When a strong classical baseline already captures most structure, LLM evolution often produces bounded refinement rather than a dominant new method.
meta_patterns.pattern: Improvement depends on available benchmark headroom.

meta_patterns.evidence: The game loop mainly exposed action/runtime behavior issues, TSP exposed replay-policy sensitivity, and CVRP exposed feasibility/scoring pressure plus low acceptance rates.
meta_patterns.interpretation: A unified framework should classify failure by domain-specific validator pressure rather than only by code novelty or final score.
meta_patterns.pattern: Failure modes shift with domain constraints.

meta_patterns.evidence: Codex direct CVRP held-out gap was 0.06778; phase-9 evolved mean held-out gap was 0.182231; Clarke-Wright was 0.073766.
meta_patterns.interpretation: The current data support a framework of capabilities and limits, not a claim that LLM evolution beats mature optimization heuristics.
meta_patterns.pattern: The strongest defensible story is capability-bounded adaptation.
